## 1. The life of this world like rain  (`#life-like-rain`)

Cited ayat: 10:24, 18:45, 57:20

> **10:24** إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلْأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَخَذَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ وَظَنَّ أَهْلُهَآ أَنَّهُمْ قَٰدِرُونَ عَلَيْهَآ أَتَىٰهَآ أَمْرُنَا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهَارًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهَا حَصِيدًا كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ بِٱلْأَمْسِ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

> **18:45** وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّيَٰحُ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مُّقْتَدِرًا

> **57:20** ٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌۢ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِى ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَوْلَٰدِ كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ ٱلْكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَٰمًا وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنٌ وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلْغُرُورِ

### Claims

**c1** (10:24): The ayah says that the similitude of the life of this world is like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth, from which people and cattle eat, mingled, until the earth took its adornment and was adorned, and its people thought they were able over it, then His command came to it by night or by day, and He made it a reaped field, as if it had not been there the day before.

**c2** (10:24): The ayah adds that thus God makes the signs clear for a people who reflect.

**c3** (18:45): The ayah commands that a similitude of the life of this world be struck for them: like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled, and it became dry stubble that the winds scatter; and God has power over all things.

**c4** (57:20): The ayah says to know that the life of this world is play, amusement, adornment, boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children, like a rain whose growth pleased the kuffar; then it dries, and you see it yellow, then it becomes broken stubble.

**c5** (57:20): The ayah adds that in the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval, and that the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion.

### One-minute summary

The ayat in different surahs liken the life of this world to rain and to what grows from it, which then becomes a reaped field, dry stubble or broken stubble [c1][c3][c4]. The last of them adds that in the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval [c5].

### Complete story

In one ayah, the similitude of the life of this world is like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled [c1]. The earth took its adornment and was adorned, and its people thought they were able over it, then His command came to it by night or by day, and He made it a reaped field, as if it had not been there the day before [c1]. Thus God makes the signs clear for a people who reflect [c2].

In another ayah, a similitude of the life of this world is to be struck for them, like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled [c3]. It became dry stubble that the winds scatter, and God has power over all things [c3].

In a further ayah, the life of this world is play, amusement, adornment, boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children [c4]. It is like a rain whose growth pleased the kuffar; then it dries, and you see it yellow, then it becomes broken stubble [c4]. In the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval, and the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion [c5].

### Deep study

The ayat share the picture of water from the sky and the plants that grow with it, and each ends it differently: a reaped field, dry stubble scattered by the winds, and broken stubble [c1][c3][c4]. Only 10:24 and 18:45 speak of a similitude by that word, while 57:20 compares the life of this world to rain with the word like and lists what it is [c1][c3][c4]. The word kuffar in 57:20 is read as the disbelievers or as the farmers, and the ayah does not settle it [c4].

### Kids mode

The ayat say that the life of this world is like rain from the sky, and like the plants that grow with it [c1][c3]. The plants later become dry stubble [c3]. God has power over all things [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat compare the life of this world to rain and to what grows from it, which then dries and is scattered or broken [c1][c3][c4]. Another reading is that the last ayah sets the life of this world beside the hereafter, where there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whether the ayat are statements of one similitude or separate similitudes; they come from different surahs and the ayat do not say.
- Not established: when the reaping or the drying takes place; 10:24 says by night or by day, and no more.
- The word kuffar in 57:20 is read as disbelievers or as farmers; this draft keeps the Arabic word.
- The ayat 10:24 and 18:45 use the word for a similitude (mathal); 57:20 gives a likeness with the word like and states what the life of this world is.
